Two mornings here

Five in the morning

Somebody is already pouring.

Before the school buses, before the mill shift, before anything else on this road is awake — the little window is open and the first cup of the day is going out.

Watch it come together

The cup on every lid and every cup sleeve out that window — drawn, poured, and spotted, the way one actually gets made.

The stand

One small building, run by two people.

Jenn and Brandon run Farmhouse Brew out of one small building at the top of Black Diamond — a drive-thru with a door, a few tables and a cactus by the step.

It pours Dillano's, a Washington roaster, and everything else on the board is built to order at a window you can reach from the driver's seat. Regulars get remembered — the reviews are full of people whose drink was already started by the time they pulled up.

“The people working here are amazing — they recommend the best drinks. My favorite coffee stand.”— a Google review

Find us

Third Ave, north end of town.

  1. Pull in

    The gravel lot wraps the stand — the drive-thru lane runs down the side, and there's parking if you'd rather walk up.

  2. Order at the window

    Everything on the board is made to order. Say what you want on it; the answer is usually yes.

  3. Take a table, or take it with you

    There's seating out front for the days that deserve it.
